splice.note: whole SEQ_030 row: K_R6_030_MID (drawing unrolled, no glow yet) to K_R6_030_END (glow drawn); enters through the night-to-morning dip

plan.environment: the same grey-walled dining hall in the morning: one long wooden table down the left side with brown chairs and children's drawings along it, barred windows on the left wall, a tiled counter with a steel cooking pot on the right, a bright open doorway at the far end
plan.emotional_guidance: Valence: determined, proud. Arousal: gentle, building steadily as the glow grows.
plan.visual_style: finished full-colour 3D animation, identical in look, lighting and character design to the first frame; never a sketch

audio.sounds: P01 quick crayon scribbles scratching on paper, faster and larger; P02 the small tap and roll of a crayon on the wood; P03 a faint chair creak as the crayon boy leans in; unpitched foley only, no tones, no melody
audio.room: the morning hall, bright and calm, the other children drawing at a distance

panels.video_beat: morning: Maria sits in her seat at the long table with her drawing unrolled flat in front of her, holds it down with one hand and picks up an orange crayon; the crayon boy beyond her draws on his own sheet

Maria scribbles big warm yellow and orange glow all around the drawn robot, thickest around its chest, again and again, the glow growing bigger while the crayon boy beyond her keeps drawing on his own sheet
the glow scribbles spread and run off the top, right and bottom edges of the paper onto the wooden table in a few streaks; Maria keeps scribbling with her orange crayon
the crayon boy leans in from his seat beyond her to look at the glowing drawing, his hands on the table edge; Maria's hand is still scribbling at the last moment

plan.continuity: Maria in the second window-side seat in profile at the left; the crayon boy in the seat beyond her; the same camera from the first frame to the last; one drawing only, Maria's, the same family drawing, the glow growing around the drawn robot
preventions: the grey hall of the first frame, never a hall with a red porthole door or a bulletin board
Maria's drawing keeps one design, size and orientation in every frame: the girl, the dog with the blue checked blanket and the robot together, never a robot alone
no other sheet shows a robot
one of each person, no lookalike girl and no second boy in a green shirt
the camera does not move away from the first frame's view; the drawing never leaves the table

design: one-clip SEQ_030 (15 s) from K_R6_030_MID to K_R6_030_END, replacing plan A's establishing start frame, which failed review twice (a1 robot sheet, a2 a second Maria)
